title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 13 and 15). A 'model' X = (L, S, ∂) is a combinatorial model of a 1-dimensional topological shape. L is a set of points. S ⊂ P(L) is a family of 'segments'. ∂ : S → P_2(L) assigns to each segment its two endpoints. For x ∈ L, B_x is the set of 'bandes' (branches, i.e. germs of segments at x). In a regular model B_x has two elements, as for a point of a 1-manifold. On p.13 Grothendieck reduces regular models to connected regular ones. For a connected regular model he states a theorem: there is a transitive system of bijections among all the ∂I (I ∈ S) and all the B_x (x ∈ L). This yields a single 2-element set ω, with compatible isomorphisms ω ≃ ∂I and ω ≃ B_x.

This page states the conditions that determine the system.
(a) Compatibility with inclusion. Let J ⊂ I and let o be one of the two canonical total orders on I. Then o restricts to a canonical order on J. The bijection ∂I ≃ ∂J sends min_o(I) to min_o(J), and hence max to max (use the opposite order).
(b) Compatibility with branches. If x0 ∈ ∂I is the smallest element for a canonical order o on I, then under ∂I ≃ B_{x0} the element x0 corresponds to the branch β(I, x0) that I defines at x0.

The construction is then made precise. Take the disjoint union ∐_{I∈S} ∂I ∐ ∐_{x∈L} B_x and the equivalence relation R generated by two elementary relations:
- (I,x) ~_a (J,y) when J ⊂ I and x, y correspond under the order matching;
- (I,x) ~_b (x, β(I,x)) for x ∈ ∂I.
One must show that R has exactly two classes. Page 15 adds that the two endpoints of any one segment must lie in different classes. Grothendieck is unsure whether this follows from the axioms or must be imposed as one.

The quotient set ω is the set of orientations of X. Choosing an element of ω orients X: every segment gets an origin and every point an outgoing germ. This feeds the next step (p.15). There he defines x ≺ y iff some segment has origin x and extremity y, and splits into the linear case (≺ transitive, so a preorder) and the circular case. In modern terms, this page builds the orientation double cover / orientation set of a connected combinatorial 1-manifold as π0 of a generated equivalence relation, i.e. a groupoid/local-system argument done by hand.
errors: Not an error but a gap, acknowledged by Grothendieck on the next page: nothing on this page proves that R has at most two classes or that the two endpoints of a segment are not identified. 'At most two' needs connectedness plus a propagation argument along chains of overlapping segments. 'Not identified' is an orientability/consistency statement. For genuine 1-dimensional shapes it is true, but in the abstract axiom system it may have to be assumed.

Condition (b) uses an order-dependent convention: the minimum is matched to the branch pointing into I. Consistency of (b) with (a) when J ⊂ I share the endpoint x0 must be checked: β(J,x0) should equal β(I,x0). Presumably this is part of the regularity axioms on p.12-13, but it is not verified here.

ideas.what: Axiomatic combinatorial model (L, S, ∂) of 1-dimensional topological shapes via points, segments with two-point boundaries, and branches B_x
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial/order-theoretic models of 1-manifolds and graphs; tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: various (betweenness geometry, ordered and cyclically ordered sets; o-minimal / tame topology of van den Dries et al.)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology ('topologie modérée') is announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but this specific formalism appears unpublished

ideas.what: Orientation set ω of a connected regular model, constructed as the quotient of ∐∂I ∐ ∐B_x by the equivalence relation generated by inclusion-compatibility and branch-compatibility
ideas.modern_name: orientation double cover / orientation torsor as π0 of a groupoid (connected components of the orientation local system)

ideas.what: Matching of endpoints of nested segments through restriction of canonical orders

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open whether 'R has exactly two classes and separates the endpoints of each segment' is a theorem of the regularity axioms or must be added as an axiom. This is part of an unpublished axiomatization of 1-dimensional 'formes' that later leads to the linear/circular dichotomy via transitivity of the filiation relation.
missed.quote: Il faut voir que la relation d'équivalence R ... admet exactement deux classes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor open point in a self-contained, purely combinatorial foundation for 1-dimensional tame topology. Such foundations could be compared with cyclic orders, the cyclic category Λ, and o-minimal 1-dimensional structures. Its mathematical content, however, is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out the classical orientation double-cover construction inside Grothendieck's unpublished combinatorial axiomatics for 1-dimensional shapes. The framework itself (part of the 1986 'géométrie des formes' tame-topology project) is little known, but this page's content is routine.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 insertion is probably a marginal addition ('données ... quant à un des I') relating to the isomorphisms ∂I ≃ ...; the reading is uncertain.
In (a) the condition is J ⊂ I (written 'I ⊃ J'), and the surviving text reads 'des ordres canoniques sur I, associe au plus petit élément de I le plus petit élément de J'.
In (b) read: 'alors [dans ∂I ≃ B_{x0}] à x0 ∈ ∂I correspond la bande qu'on a définie par I'. The word read 'la[?] bande[?]' is likely 'dans' or a reference to the isomorphism.
'par la jonction[?]' is uncertain; it likely refers to the correspondence described in (a), e.g. 'par la première flèche' or 'par la fonction'.
The struck '$R_a\ R_b$' after '(a), (b)' is correctly marked as deleted.
The circled subscripts under ~ are (a) and (b), and 'x ∈ ∂I' is written beneath the pairs (I,x).
